source: He berated and insulted me, Mother. The murderer under our noses. He tricked me.
Claudius is a vile, vile man. He tried to threaten my life. How my days must be numbered now!
Y-your life? Claudius?
I thought it might be worth standing up to that villainy. But there's no point. Why must violence beget more violence so endlessly?
Time to rid the world of one more pile of human filth.
No, no, no, no!
This-- This isn't real, is it?
I know he'll be alive again soon enough, but that doesn't matter now.
Because of that performance he saw, I hurt him so much.
Soon he will have no memory of his pain.
But here, right now, I caused him to take his own life. That he will retain no memory of the death doesn't make it right.
No. It makes it 'nothing.' Neither right nor wrong. It is meaningless. Rid yourself of guilt. You will need all wits about you if you are to prevail.
How can you say that?
I will never see their deaths as nothing.
Sometimes necessary, maybe. I learned a lot here, today. But never 'nothing.'
His suffering was real. And his blood is on my hands.
We shall see how your opinion evolves as your time spent in this world does.
Next time around, perhaps, will be different.
I hurt him so much.
I couldn't help you this time, Hamlet. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.
Lady Birgitta!
Brit! Oh, come, now. Don't look so surprised!
Did you miss me?
Shouldn't you be on the sea by now?
Couldn't stay away from you. As always.
So you're, what? You've returned?
Mmm... indefinitely delayed my departure, more like.
My family needs me close right now. My sister especially.
Oh, come on. 'Feely can't be without her big brother for one little summer?
Don't call her that.
Fine. I won't. But you're tense. What's really going on, Laertes?
We'll talk about it tonight. When we're alone, away from prying eyes.
I will see you tonight, yes?
Of course. Always, love.
So much for your time in Paris.
I received some news from home which couldn't be ignored.
I'm sorry about your father.
So am I. Someone must bury him, and here I am.
My father was not perfect. But he was kind, and his heart was noble, and I pray that I do his name justice in the future.
Might I visit you later?
My chambers.
I'll think on it. I suppose the least I can do is entertain the invitation.
It's not often you invite me into your chambers, where anyone might see us.
And it's even less often I would entertain such an invitation at all. Just so we're perfectly clear.
Fickle as your heart is, it is fond of me. This, I know.
You fool. Why didn't you go to Paris?
Maybe then you would've found a girl you could actually wed.
You fool. Why didn't you stay in Paris?
I wish with all my heart your father were still alive, and you had stayed in Paris.
Perhaps then you'd have had the summer you deserved.
And you would've found a girl you could actually wed.
You already know how I feel about that. Besides...
I'm worried for you.
I heard you were unwell, and I came to find you.
'Unwell?' Hmph! Who told you that?
She mentioned you were out of sorts. Acting strangely. I told her I hadn't noticed.
Of course, men never notice these things.
Needless to say, these last few months have been some of the darkest of my life.
Thankfully, your sister changed that.
Yes. I owe her. More than you'll ever know.
Did your sister put you up to this?
She's been awfully friendly lately. Trying to perform all sorts of feats on my behalf.
N-not at all!
You're a horrible liar.
It's been months, Laertes. I still haven't heard from her.
Your mother?
Yes. She promised she'd write to me each month. And... now... nothing.
I must assume she finds me wretched, or is displeased with me somehow.
I've spent each day wracking my mind trying to think of why. And I just can't.
You haven't received one letter? Wasn't the Queen to make sure you received them?
Yes. But she hasn't brought me anything.
In the meantime, I sit, and I thread needles and I read Latin and I advise my lady on her choice of dress and—
It's all meaningless, Laertes. All of it.
It's not meaningless, Brit.
What of your art? Have you found a desire to create lately?
Perhaps. If I had the means to do so. But I haven't.
And that ugly little town outside the castle has nothing of use to me.
It's nothing like Copenhagen, where the masters throw their workshop doors wide in the summertime.
Have you spoken to Horatio? I believe he's an artist of sorts. He might be of use to you.
Perhaps. Perhaps I might. It just seems pointless.
I shall die here. Or else become someone else's pawn. Just a carved figure they can push around however they like.
Anyhow. Enough of the macabre. So glad to know my despair is castle gossip now.
Well, I heard something else. Something strange. But it didn't ring entirely false, either.
Brit, I heard something strange. But it didn't ring entirely false, either.
I see. And you think I can echo it.
Well, you're uncannily good at it, aren't you? But this rumor must remain in absolute confidence.
Of course, love. You have my word. You always do.
Do you think there's any chance King Claudius might have murdered his brother?
Are you serious?
W-well, I did think it sounded far-fetched.
No, I think it's absolutely true!
At least, I think so. I've absolutely no proof to that extent. But I can only imagine he did.
Haven't you seen the official death report in the gallery? It's ludicrous.
You think it's true? If it is...
Then he's fully gotten away with his crime.
Then Claudius died having gotten away with his crime. And he's gone now, so I suppose it doesn't matter.
Just another way our country is poisoned.
I'm far less concerned. Murder is a tool. Those who wear a crown must use it, and use it well.
If he killed King Hamlet, it's only because his expertise with that tool was defter than King Hamlet's.
Well, not everyone feels as secure as you do, I'm afraid.
Sadly, you're not the only person I'm worried about.
My sister believes someone wants to hurt her.
Ultimately, that's the real reason I didn't go to Paris. I couldn't. Not after seeing her face.
Ophelia thinks someone wants to hurt her? For what reason?
I'm not certain. I know how it sounds. But I believe her.
You've always got your ear to the ground when it comes to gossip within the castle.
Does anyone harbor ill will towards Ophelia? Anyone who would want to cause her trouble or frighten her?
I think you ought to watch Ophelia's back.
If you don't watch over her, what Claudius did to his brother could happen again with her.
If you don't watch over her, Claudius might...
That's what she spoke to me about. What I don't understand is why.
You think the King might harm her? That's quite an assertion.
Think a moment. She broke Hamlet's heart, and he's still smitten with her powerfully.
He watches her like a lovesick fool. The King believes it's what's driven him mad.
If Hamlet were to do something foolish, such as ask for her hand in marriage...
Then Claudius couldn't use him to make political allegiances any longer.
And he isn't a popular King. He needs all the ties he can make.
Hamlet's been harassing her. Against all possible wisdom, of course.
You think Hamlet might harm her?
I don't know. In the worst case scenario, Hamlet might become violent.
And in the best case scenario, the lovesick idiot might ask her to marry him, and she might consent.
She seems to be coming apart at the seams somewhat.
I worry that with your father dead, something has changed in her. She's been asking all manner of odd questions.
I worry that with Hamlet dead, something has changed in her. She's been asking all manner of odd questions.
Ophelia told me about a strange thing she heard.
She said that you had asked her to facilitate a meeting between you and Hamlet.
Is that something your father asked you to do?
The King and my father both want me to marry Hamlet so that House Brockenhuus will align with Elsinore's intentions.
Surely you can't mean your father would just give you over to him! Against your will, too!
I think it's possible.
My father will do as he pleases. I am merely his extension. A tool.
That's horrid.
It isn't what you want. Not at all. Or is it?
Laertes, you know how I feel. Would that my fate were my own...
You and I would...
But, well, look. There's no sense in dwelling on all this.
Besides, we must celebrate you being here. With me.
And here I thought you weren't the sort to be romantic, or something of the like.
If you don't hush, I'm going to turn right around and leave again.
(Laertes is--)
(And Brit is--)
(I can't even look. I need something to block the sounds out.)
(Oh no. Not again.)
Before I go, there's something that's on my mind.
Isn't there always?
You said Ophelia asked you to come speak to me.
She did.
That explains it, then.
Reveal yourself, you little pervert. I can hear you mouth breathing.
Who are you talking t--
I can explain.
How creepy you are? Don't worry, we're thoroughly aware.
I knew something wasn't right with you, Brit. I thought my brother could... help you.
I wanted to make things better for you.
Because I know how hard they've been lately.
Why would you...
Great. Just great.
It's so fittingly self-centered that your reaction to 'Please leave me alone, Ophelia, I don't want to become friends' was to try and do even more.
Maybe after I've actually had that drink, I'll be able to better explain how insufferable you are.
No. No. I don't believe you. You're lying to me. You must be. You must want something.
I assure you it's no trick. I don't want anything. Just to be on friendly terms.
You think you can run a couple errands and suddenly we're bosom-born sisters? Y-you... you...
Leave me alone! I don't want to be friends. With anyone in this castle. Has that ever occurred to you? That I don't need you?
What if you get to know me and you don't even like the real me? The person I really am? You'll just be disappointed.
